body.x: A drug screening in the field depends on a person squinting at a test strip, and two people can read the same faint line differently. For a result that may be used in law enforcement, that variability is a weakness.

COSMAS Bioscience, Inc., a company in Gwanak-gu, Seoul, aims to eliminate the uncertainty of visual interpretation. Led by CEO Hojeong Yu, the company will take part in Korea Police World Expo 2026 (KPEX 2026), where it will show D-FREE, a field-deployable drug testing system that uses saliva.

COSMAS Bioscience, founded in 2024, says it specializes in high-sensitivity, rapid point-of-care diagnostic platforms and is currently focused on an integrated drug testing system for law enforcement and public safety. According to the company, its core technology combines a high-sensitivity saliva-based test kit, a compact portable optical reader and an on-device AI automated interpretation algorithm. The reader measures subtle optical signals from the kit and the AI analyzes and interprets them, which the company says overcomes the limits of visual interpretation, reduces differences between operators and makes results more objective and reliable.

D-FREE, the company says, uses a multiplex saliva kit that screens at the same time for five major drugs, including THC, methamphetamine, morphine, oxycodone and MDMA. It names four advantages: multiplex screening, AI-powered automated interpretation, high-sensitivity signal analysis and field usability. Because it pairs saliva testing with compact portable equipment, COSMAS says, D-FREE can be used quickly and conveniently in police enforcement and other public safety settings. The company says it aims to develop the system into a scalable on-site screening platform that can adapt quickly to emerging and novel drugs.

COSMAS says D-FREE is approaching commercialization and that it is carrying out validation to assess field applicability and commercial potential based on its core technologies and prototype development. In 2027, it plans to run field validation with the Korea National Police Agency to evaluate test performance, interpretation accuracy, user convenience and overall operability in real law enforcement settings. Based on the results, it intends to seek regulatory approval in Korea and the United States, through the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). It also plans to show D-FREE at CES 2027 to reach international buyers and partners.

The company's goals at the exhibition are to introduce D-FREE to potential end users in law enforcement and public safety, gather feedback on their requirements and on real-world applicability, and find potential customers, distribution and business partners and strategic collaborators for its expansion into domestic and global public safety and drug screening markets.

COSMAS has no overseas sales yet, but it names the United States as its top-priority market and says it is preparing to enter. It points to a large U.S. market for drug screening and point-of-care diagnostics and strong demand for fast, accurate, portable field tests. After the United States, it plans to move into other major markets including Europe and China, and it expects demand for rapid and objective on-site drug screening to grow as illicit drug distribution and new psychoactive substances increase worldwide. The company is looking for local distributors of drug testing products, partners experienced in working with law enforcement agencies and organizations that can support regulatory approval and market entry, with the aim of building a framework that connects local validation, approval, distribution and business development.

Its plans are to strengthen D-FREE through further development and field validation with the Korea National Police Agency while preparing for approvals at home and abroad, to prioritize the United States for local validation and commercialization before Europe and China, and to work with local distributors and partners with experience in law enforcement agencies, pilot adoption and distribution networks. It also intends to use global exhibitions, such as CES 2027, to continue finding overseas buyers and to shape market-entry strategies for each country.

The company expects three difficulties: differences in regulatory and approval requirements for drug testing products between countries, securing opportunities for local field validation, and finding reliable distribution and business partners. It says country-specific regulatory consulting, connections with local public agencies and validation partners, buyer and distributor matching, participation in international exhibitions and follow-up business development support would help.

Korea Police World Expo 2026 (KPEX 2026) is hosted by the Korea National Police Agency and Incheon Metropolitan City and organized by the Incheon Tourism Organization, MESSE ESANG Co., Ltd. and KOTRA. It runs from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at Songdo Convensia in Incheon. The show pairs a Police Expo covering mobility and robotics, personal protective equipment and counter-terrorism, crime investigation and forensic equipment, traffic equipment and systems, and training and support solutions, with a Security Expo covering cybercrime prevention and response, video security, access control, and public safety and integrated control.
